headline: Anthropic's threat report and the AI-agent swarm that breached 395 PaperCut users put machine-run intrusions at the center of the day, while GitLab, JFrog Artifactory, and ScreenConnect flaws drew exploitation within hours of disclosure.

emerging_trends.text: Anthropic's Generative Threat Groups report and the PaperCut swarm arrived the same day, and both show attackers handing routine intrusion labor to commercial models, from rebuilding malware after each detection to farming secrets out of 1.8 million Android apps to running reconnaissance and exfiltration across 395 organizations.
emerging_trends.topic_title: PaperCut Ships Maintenance Releases After AI-Agent Campaign

emerging_trends.text: Exploitation now trails disclosure by hours: probes hit GitLab's maximum-severity file-read bug the day it went public, and CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog picked up JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and GitLab entries within a single morning.
emerging_trends.topic_title: GitLab and Check Point Ship Critical Patches

emerging_trends.text: ShinyHunters keeps reaching enterprise data through people: the gang lifted a police employee's stored credentials off a personal device to open Florida's DAVID driver database, and Microsoft watched the same crews talk staff into passkey enrollments that surrender Microsoft 365 mailboxes.

topics.title: Criminals Point Claude at Malware Evasion
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic published the full threat report behind yesterday's disclosure, naming the clusters Generative Threat Groups and covering December 2025 through August 2026: GTG-20006, which aligns with the Russian state-sponsored group Midnight Blizzard, used Claude to rebuild malware each time defenders detected it and ran the campaign against more than 20 government, intelligence, diplomatic, and defense organizations; another group pointed Claude at 1.8 million Android applications and pulled hardcoded secrets out of them; other groups used the models for weapons design, propaganda, and mass surveillance; and Anthropic separately disrupted industrial-scale distillation attacks from seven China-based labs, among them Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Z.ai, and MiniMax, that pumped its models to extract capabilities into their own. Dark Reading documented a fraud crew that generated 1 million personalized scam emails in three days, ending the old trade-off between volume and credibility.
topics.summary: Attackers now fold commercial models into ordinary espionage and criminal work, using them to mutate malware past detection engines and to write convincing executive impersonations, and they treat the model vendors themselves as targets worth breaching. Finance teams should confirm every payment-detail change through a channel separate from email.

topics.title: PaperCut Ships Maintenance Releases After AI-Agent Campaign
topics.latest_developments: PaperCut released maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13, and 24.1.10 that replace every emergency patch the company had pushed for the two actively exploited flaws, and GreyNoise detailed the attacker's method: a private lab holding a vulnerable copy of PaperCut NG/MF and an Active Directory domain, where the suspected Russian-speaking operator built and tested the exploit before handing the break-ins to AI agents that reached at least 440 instances at 395 organizations in 48 countries; Dark Reading traced the agents through the whole kill chain, from staging the lab to reconnaissance, lateral movement, and exfiltration.
topics.summary: PaperCut NG/MF runs print management for schools, universities, and enterprises worldwide, and the exploited pair chains an authentication bypass with remote code execution. Administrators should move straight to 26.0.5, 25.0.13, or 24.1.10 and hunt for unfamiliar accounts and outbound connections to 45.142.193.132.

topics.title: GitLab and Check Point Ship Critical Patches
topics.latest_developments: CISA added CVE-2026-85706 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 11, 2026, the 10.0-rated path traversal bug in GitLab's repository commits API that lets an unauthenticated user read any file on the server and that drew in-the-wild probes within hours of the September 10 disclosure; Check Point assigned CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103 to the two critical VPN certificate handling flaws in its Security Gateways and Security Management products that yield remote code execution.
topics.summary: GitLab holds the source code and continuous integration pipelines of the companies that run it, and Check Point gateways terminate corporate VPN traffic, so both sit where one flaw opens everything behind it. Administrators should apply each vendor's fix immediately.

topics.title: Intruders Backdoor Unpatched JFrog Artifactory Servers
topics.latest_developments: CISA added the two Artifactory flaws behind the campaign, the incorrect authorization bug CVE-2026-42016 and the improper authentication bug CVE-2026-42018, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 11, 2026, alongside CVE-2026-84869, a ConnectWise ScreenConnect privilege management flaw that attackers also exploit; BleepingComputer identified the payload the intruders plant on self-hosted Artifactory servers as a Rust backdoor, and Wiz dated the attacks from August 15 through September 8, 2026 and found they reached only the servers whose operators had skipped JFrog's earlier fixes.
topics.summary: Artifactory holds the packages that software build pipelines pull from, so a backdoor there reaches every application a company ships. Operators of self-hosted Artifactory should apply JFrog's fixes, audit administrator accounts, and inspect stored artifacts for tampering.

topics.title: Conti Sentence and Treasury's Scam Reporting Push
topics.latest_developments: Oleksii Oleksiyovych Lytvynenko, the Ukrainian national whom Irish authorities arrested in 2023, drew four years in a U.S. prison for developing Conti ransomware, an operation that hit more than 1,000 victims worldwide before shutting down in 2022; the U.S. Department of the Treasury urged banks to file more reports on cyber-enabled scams, tallying nearly $13 billion in losses since 2023 as scam compounds expand worldwide; and CISA joined a new government advisory pressing organizations toward plainer breach notification and incident response practices as outages mount.
topics.summary: Treasury wants banks to feed it more detail on what happens to defrauded customers, the raw material for sanctions and seizures against the Southeast Asian and African compounds. Banks should route scam cases into suspicious activity reports rather than closing them as ordinary fraud.

topics.title: Cisco Firewall Flaws Deliver Qilin Ransomware
topics.latest_developments: Sophos identified the malware riding one of the intrusion clusters as Cyclops Blink, the modular implant Russia's Sandworm group deployed against network devices years ago, now rebuilt with new capabilities and aimed at Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center appliances; Cisco Talos had already named the payoff behind the three clusters exploiting CVE-2026-20079, the 10.0-rated authentication bypass in the Secure Firewall Management Center web interface, and CVE-2026-20316, which steal credentials and then deploy Qilin ransomware.
topics.summary: Secure Firewall Management Center sets policy for Cisco firewalls, so an unauthenticated bypass there hands an attacker the perimeter and the credentials the appliance holds. CISA gave federal civilian agencies until September 12, 2026 to patch; every other operator should install Cisco's fixes and rotate stored credentials now.

topics.title: ShinyHunters Opens Florida's DAVID Driver Database
topics.latest_developments: The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles confirmed that attackers breached DAVID, the driver and vehicle information database that Florida law enforcement queries, using credentials a police department employee had stored on a personal device, and the cybercrime group ShinyHunters claims the theft; Microsoft reported the same day that ShinyHunters, Helix, and other extortion crews now run passkey and single sign-on themed social engineering to take over corporate Microsoft accounts and pull data out of Microsoft 365.
topics.summary: DAVID holds Florida driver photographs, addresses, and license records, and one officer's saved password opened it. Agencies that grant employees access to state record systems should require phishing-resistant authentication and bar credential storage on personal phones and laptops.

topics.title: Attackers Turn AI Platforms Into Delivery Infrastructure
topics.latest_developments: Huntress documented criminals hosting malware lures inside weaponized Claude Artifacts, shared AI chat transcripts, and sponsored search results, poisoning search results for people looking for AI tools and pushing ClickFix-style prompts; the SANS Internet Storm Center traced an attacker running a semi-autonomous coding agent that hunts poorly secured large language model resale gateways, farms accounts and exploits ordinary web flaws to take API access, validates the capacity, and aggregates the stolen inference behind a gateway of their own; and Ars Technica reported ClickFix infections spreading on both Windows and macOS.
topics.summary: ClickFix tells a victim to paste a command into a terminal or Run dialog to fix a fake error, and the lure now arrives dressed as legitimate AI content on platforms users already trust. Tell staff to treat any web page that asks them to paste a command as an attack, and check whether your own LLM gateways demand authentication.

sources.title: How Threat Actors Are Turning Trusted AI Platforms Into an Attack Surface

topics.title: UNC3569 Rides Sogou Input Method to GRAYRABBIT
topics.latest_developments: Gen Digital published research on September 10, 2026 showing that the China-linked group UNC3569 exploited a flaw in Sogou Input Method, the Tencent-owned tool that ranks among the most widely used ways to type Chinese characters on Windows, starting each intrusion with a crafted link and finishing with a backdoor called GRAYRABBIT that carries the logged-in user's full rights.
topics.summary: Sogou Input Method sits on millions of Windows desktops and loads into every application that accepts typing, which makes it an unusually quiet foothold. Organizations with Chinese-language users should inventory Sogou installations and update them.

sources.title: China-Linked UNC3569 Exploited Sogou Input Method Flaw to Deploy GRAYRABBIT Backdoor

around_teams.title: Fittipaldo and McCarthy Close Out Week 1 Prep
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette beat writer Ray Fittipaldo posted his Steelers chat transcript Thursday, September 10, and head coach Mike McCarthy met the media the same day before practice.
around_teams.summary: Fittipaldo took reader questions on the Week 1 roster and the Atlanta matchup, and McCarthy spoke on the Steelers' own channel three days before kickoff. The Steelers host the Falcons at 1 p.m. Sunday, September 13, on FOX.

around_teams.title: Hiles Puts the Standard on McCarthy
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles wrote Friday, September 11, that setting a new Steelers standard ranks as head coach Mike McCarthy's top priority in his first season.
around_teams.summary: McCarthy takes over a franchise that has gone years without a playoff win, and Hiles argues the measure of 2026 lies in the habits and expectations McCarthy installs rather than the win total, starting with Sunday's opener against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: Setting the new Steelers standard should be Mike McCarthy's top priority this season

around_teams.title: Rodgers Savors a Last Season
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Thursday, September 10, that quarterback Aaron Rodgers plans to savor what he calls a special season in Pittsburgh as his career winds down.
around_teams.summary: Rodgers, who opens his second year with the Steelers on Sunday, September 13, against the Atlanta Falcons, has told teammates and reporters he treats this run as the end of the line, and he spoke with the media at practice Wednesday, September 9, alongside DK Metcalf, Alex Highsmith, and Eli Heidenreich a day later.

team_usa.title: Lawson's Message Carries the U.S. Into the Semifinals
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Friday, September 11, that the United States women believe coach Kara Lawson's demands have them peaking as they enter the FIBA World Cup semifinals in Germany.
team_usa.summary: The Americans reached the semifinals by routing Hungary 108-56 in Thursday's quarterfinal, their 34th straight World Cup win, and Lawson has pushed the team to improve round by round after a 55-52 escape against Italy in pool play.

sources.title: Team USA takes Lawson's message to heart entering World Cup semis
Chemistry building for U.S., into FIBA semis after Hungary rout

team_usa.title: Pulisic Chafes on the Milan Bench
team_usa.latest_developments: AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim said Friday, September 11, that Christian Pulisic is upset about sitting out so far this season, and hinted the American will play this weekend.
team_usa.summary: Pulisic, the United States men's national team forward, has yet to feature for Milan in the new Serie A season, and Amorim addressed the situation publicly before the club's next match.

sources.title: Pulisic 'upset' about Milan bench role, coach Amorim says

team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN surveyed Friday, September 11, the American men who missed this year's World Cup squad and now aim at the 2030 tournament.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Superintelligence is a Fairy Tale. But Chasing It Can Still Cause Harm.
reading.summary: Newport answers Anthropic employees who said publicly that the systems they build could kill billions, arguing that superintelligence remains a story people tell themselves. He holds that the race toward it still does real damage, in the resources it consumes and the harms it creates along the way.
